label: B2B software with a retention curve
note: Type the values in and paste this curve into the custom retention box. The correct result is a fully loaded cost per customer of about $4,082, payback near 6.2 months and LTV to CAC of about 4.1.

label: Subscription box with a spreadsheet curve
note: The curve is pasted with percent signs the way a spreadsheet exports it. Check that the tool used it: the correct payback is about 13.1 months, not the 7.8 you get from the churn field alone.

label: Dealer subscriptions, mostly organic
note: Only 18 of 60 new dealers came from paid media. The cost per paid dealer is $3,000, not $900, so judge payback on the fully loaded figure (about 6.1 months).

label: One-time purchase retailer
note: Customers buy once, so enter churn 100 and the curve "100". The result of no payback within 12 months is right, and the tool has no repeat-purchase model to show more.

label: Retention curve, clean
note: A simple retention curve with one percent value per month. It should be read as written.

label: Retention curve, tabs and percent signs
note: A curve pasted from a spreadsheet with tabs and percent signs. If results look the same as with no curve, the paste was not read, so retype it with commas.

label: Retention curve as fractions
note: Values like 0.71 mean 71 percent. Entered as is they are read as under 1 percent, so multiply by 100 first.

label: Curve that rises at the end
note: Retention goes up in the last month (60, 40, then 45). Extending that trend inflates lifetime value, so fix the tail before trusting the result.
